articleTitle: ELM Based Composite Anti-Disturbance Control of a Class of Nonlinear Systems based on Disturbance Observer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: This paper studies the design problem of extreme learning machine (ELM) based composite anti-disturbance control for a class of nonlinear systems with disturbances modeled by nonlinear exogenous system. First, the ELM network is used to approximate the nonlinear functions in the system and the exosystem. To deal with the disturbance of nonlinear exosystem, an ELM disturbance observer is constructed. Then, a composite anti-disturbance controller based on ELM disturbance observer is constructed to compensate the unknown disturbance. The stability of the closed loop system is analyzed. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified through the simulation experiment on the dynamic positioning system ship.

articleTitle: Regularization of Quasi -Newton Methods for Composite Multi-objective Problems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an efficient regular-ized quasi-Newton method for solving the unconstrained composite multiobjective optimization problem (UCMOP) where the objective functions are neither smooth nor convex. Under some suitable conditions, we establish that every accumulation point of the sequence produced by the proposed algorithm is a Pareto stationary point of the (UCMOP). We have conducted numerical experiments that show the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Decomposition-based Multimodal Multiobjective Algorithm Leveraging Neighborhood Information
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: The existence of multiple equivalent Pareto opti-mal sets in multimodal multiobjective optimization problems (MMOPs) poses new challenges to optimization algorithms. Despite much progress, decomposition-based algorithms have not yet fully realized their potential in solving MMOPs. This paper proposes an enhanced decomposition-based algorithm for MMOPs. The algorithm makes full use of the neighbor-hood information of the subproblems as well as the solutions in the decision space to generate high quality offspring, thus improving its convergence speed. In addition, a population pruning method is proposed to remove the less convergent solutions from the population so that computational re-sources can be used more efficiently. Experimental results show that the proposed algorithm significantly outperforms some existing algorithms in terms of overall performance in both the decision space and the objective space.

articleTitle: Convergence Analysis of the Inexact Nonmonotone Projected Gradient Method for Vector Optimization Problems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: In this paper, we put forward the inexact nonmonotone projected gradient algorithm for solving the smooth and convex vector optimization on the constrained set with regard to a fixed ordered cone. Under general assumptions, we demonstrate that the sequence produced by the algorithm has cluster points and this cluster point is a stationary point. If we consider that the objective function has <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex> -convexity, then this cluster point is also a weakly efficient point. In addition, we use the property of quasi-Fejer convergence to prove that the full sequence produced by the method in our paper converges to a weakly efficient point.

articleTitle: Construction of Knowledge Graph for Power Engineering and its Application in Digital Auditing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: With the continuous increase in the scale and complexity of power engineering projects, the number of categories involved is growing, which intensifies the challenges in auditing. To improve audit efficiency, this paper investigates methods for constructing a knowledge graph in power engineering. It effectively integrates various data types, including construction organization, construction progress, equipment status, and legal regulations, and presents the data relationships graphically. The constructed knowledge graph is equipped with intelligent retrieval and recommendation functions, which can assist auditors in swiftly identifying and analyzing abnormal risk points in power engineering projects.

articleTitle: Federated Learning-Based Social Recommendation with Social Denoising
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: In social recommendation (SR), users' social connections and behavioral data often contain sensitive information, which might lead to a deep concern about privacy leakage. In the case where raw data is absent, federated learnings social recommendation (FLSR) provide an effective framework that can not only preserve a reliable performance but also ensure the security of privacy data through collaboratively training a global model. However, existing results on FLSR often directly employ the raw interaction data without considering the impact of noise or unreliable links in social network, which may significantly decrease the effectiveness of recommendation algorithms. To address such an issue, we propose a federated learning-based social de noising recommendation (FLSDR) method consisting of three modules: graph de noising, heterogeneous graph en-coder and privacy protector. Specifically, the graph de noising module incorporates a user preference consistency function and a deletion rate to remove low-quality social connections, achieving the goal of denoising. The heterogeneous graph encoder module ensures that user embed dings are updated locally, assigning different weights to different neighbors. The privacy protection module is designed to further safeguard privacy and prevent gradient leakage of user information. Experiments over two data sets shows that our model has achieved a 4.18% improvement in performance. Ablation studies demonstrate the necessities of each component.

articleTitle: Acceleration-Level Path Tracking Scheme for Omnidirectional Mobile Robot Manipulators
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Omnidirectional mobile robot manipulators (OM-RMs) are widely used in numerous industries due to their flexi-bility and mobility. This field has attracted substantial research attention. However, current research on OMRMs primarily focus on velocity-level control, making it difficult to apply to acceleration-orientated mobile robot manipulators. This study proposes an acceleration-level path tracking scheme for the OMRM. To confirm its effectiveness, path tracking experiments are carried out on two representative trajectories. The simulation results show that the OMRM's end-effector follows the desired paths without any dispersion issues.

articleTitle: Combination Model for Sparry Calcite Intelligent Identification in Dongying Depression
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: In shale oil and gas exploration, rock structure is of paramount importance. The efficient identification of sparry calcite, which serves as an indicator of favorable lithology, is of great significance. But the logging response to sparry calcite is weak and sample sizes are limited. It is therefore difficult to accurately identify sparry calcite by conventional methods. To overcome this problem, we propose a Combination model based on data preprocessing techniques. The model utilizes conventional logging curves as the experimental data. First, the dataset is optimized by SMOTE and wavelet transforms. Subsequently, a CNN-Attention parallel network is trained to extract nonlinear features from the input logging curves. These features are then fed into the BiLSTM to extract potential information regarding the depth domain sequence. Finally, the features are summarized to achieve accurate identification of sparry calcite. The presented model is compared with CNN, BiLSTM, and CNN-BiLSTM models. The CNN-BiLSTM-Attention model provides the most favorable identification results in experiment. The combined model model possesses significant sample optimisation results and feature extraction capabilities, and it can highly efficient identification of sparry calcite in shales.

articleTitle: Reservoir Facies Modeling Based on Generative Adversarial Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Three-dimensional geological modeling of reservoirs is of great significance for developing oil and gas resources, groundwater resources, and carbon dioxide geological storage. Geological facies models are the basis for accurately predicting underground oil reservoirs, geological carbon dioxide storage potential, and groundwater resources. Traditional geostatistical modeling methods can be consistent with geological models to some extent, but there are obvious shortcomings when the characteristics of geological models become complex. Therefore, this paper takes the braided river deltaic diversion channel and estuarine dam phase of the Hanjiang Formation in the Epping Depression of the Pearl River Estuary Basin as the research objective. Based on the geological background of the workings, 3D seismic data and seven logging wells, a conditionally bounded phase simulation based on an improved GAN model is proposed. The research results show that the phase model generated by modeling well facies data matches the input well facies data. The generated phase model has good diversity, and the trained generator can generate high-quality phase models with 100%. accuracy in reproducing well facies.

articleTitle: Oilfield Production Prediction Method Based on PCA and Deep LSTM Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Oil fields have accumulated a substantial amount of data throughout the long-term production and development processes, providing a robust data foundation for machine learning applications. Addressing the challenge that simple LSTM neural networks exhibit poor predictive performance on oil field production series characterized by significant variation and fluctuation, this study first employs Principal Component Analysis (PCA) for dimensionality reduction to transform the original dataset into uncorrelated principal components. Subsequently, we optimize the architecture of the LSTM network layers and train a production prediction model. The practical application results from oil fields demonstrate that both training accuracy and prediction accuracy of the deep LSTM neural network model-trained using PCA-based dimensionality reduction-have significantly improved, with a prediction error as low as 6.47%. The developed oil field production prediction model exhibits strong generalization capabilities for production series with considerable fluctuations, enabling more accurate predictions of oil field output. This advancement holds important practical significance for the dynamic development and adjustment of oil field operations.

articleTitle: Unsupervised Military-Civilian Cross-Domain Vessel Re-Identification Using Improved Momentum Contrast Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: In this study, we introduce an unsupervised military-civilian cross-domain (UMCCD) benchmark to advance the field of vessel re-identification. By requiring models to train exclusively on unannotated civilian images and test on military images, the UMCCD benchmark rigorously assesses the models' abilities to generalize across significant domain discrepancies. To address these cross-domain challenges, we propose an improved momentum contrast learning (IMCL) method. Our IMCL method enhances the training process by increasing the number of gradient descent optimization layers while reducing the number of momentum update layers. This adjustment improves both feature representation and model robustness, crucially bridging the gap between civilian training data and military test data. Importantly, this research represents the first study to investigate unsupervised military-civilian cross-domain vessel re-identification. Our experimental results show that the IMCL method not only achieves higher accuracy but also demonstrates greater stability when compared to the MoCoV2 momentum contrast method.

articleTitle: Impact of Data Imbalance on Reservoir Fracture Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Fractures in oil and gas reservoirs are crucial for hydrocarbon storage and fluid flow, significantly affecting recovery rates. However, fracture identification is a typically imbalanced classification problem. This paper proposes a novel resampling method, Safe points-Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (Safe SMOTE), which improves upon the traditional Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) by identifying “reliable point pairs” to synthesize new minority class samples. Specifically, when nearest minority class neighbors are in a sector devoid of majority class samples, they are considered reliable point pairs, ensuring the generated samples are more representative. This approach effectively reduces the risk of misclassification for synthetic samples and enhances the accuracy of classification models. Additionally, an evaluation metric is introduced that considers both the training and testing set to better assess the resampled dataset. To validate Safe SMOTE, fracture data from Iraq's T Oilfield was analyzed. Its performance was compared with six resampling methods using Transformer (TS) and Random Forest (RF) classifiers. Additionally, the optimization and combination of two loss functions (Focal Loss (FL) and Dice Loss (DL)) were explored. The results indicated that the TS method outperformed RF overall. Furthermore, in the context of RF, the combination of Safe SMOTE with the loss functions surpassed other resampling methods. These findings further confirm the efficacy of Safe SMOTE in addressing imbalanced datasets.

articleTitle: Short-time Fourier Inversion Based Multi-band Generation for Efficient Synthetic Speech Attack
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Recent research indicates that automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems are highly susceptible to adversarial examples. Current ASR attack methods can be divided into two categories: audio-dependent and audio-independent attacks, based on whether they rely on benign audio inputs. Among them, the Speech Synthesizing based Attack (SSA), a typical audio-independent method, has gained significant attention due to its flexibility and generalizability. However, SSA suffers from low attack efficiency owing to the complex structure of the VITS decoder. To alleviate this problem, we propose a novel ASR attack method called Short-time Fourier Inversion-based Multi-band Generation (SFI-MG), which offers two main advantages. Firstly, we employ an improved inverse short-time Fourier transform (iSTFT) to optimize the traditional residual blocks, accelerating the upsampling process. Secondly, we introduce a pseudo-orthogonal mirror filter bank module to enable parallel processing across multiple frequency bands, thereby enhancing both processing speed and speech quality. Comprehensive experiments on the Common Voice, Librispeech, and VCTK datasets demonstrate that our adversarial examples not only improve attack efficiency by 210%, but also achieve a high success rate in targeted attacks.

articleTitle: Research on Training Scenario Assisted Design Method Based on Domain-Adapted Language Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: In recent years, the generative artificial intelligence technology has developed rapidly, showing great application potential in the field of training. Training scenario design requires familiarity with relevant training concepts, equipment performance, force deployment, force action and other information, and it is difficult and inefficient to rely solely on manual work. In view of this issue, we propose training scenario assisted design method based on domain-adapted language model. First, we build the training scenario question and answer database to fine-tune the large language model, then use chain of thought and retrieval-augmented to accelerate the process of training scenario design. The experimental results show that the proposed method can quickly generate the training scenario summary document and assist the relevant personnel to complete the simulation scenario design efficiently.

articleTitle: Heuristic Large-Scale Multi-Agent Path Planning with Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Multi-agent path planning is an important topic in robotics and has significant implications in autonomous vehicles and intelligent logistics. In this paper, a heuristic multi-agent path planning method is proposed. The improved channel and spatial attention modules are utilized to extract key features from the maps of agents. Then communication is conducted through the spatio-temporal Graph Transformer, enhancing coordination among agents. To improve training efficiency, the heuristic path generated by expert algorithm is designed for model training. In addition, a distance-based function is applied to assist agents in escaping deadlock situations. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method performs well in multi-agent path planning tasks across various maps.

articleTitle: Photometric Measurement Algorithm for SDSS Survey Images Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: The Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) offers extensive spectral and imaging data encompassing galactic and extragalactic objects. As a fundamental task in astronomical data analysis, photometric measurement plays a vital role in understanding the physical characteristics of celestial bodies, their evolutionary history, and the universe's large-scale structure. Traditional methods like Point Spread Function (PSF) fitting have been widely used for this purpose. However, they often face challenges such as computational inefficiency and sensitivity to noise, especially when dealing with large datasets. Consequently, a growing focus is on developing more efficient and accurate photometric measurement techniques. In this study, we introduce a deep learning model called CSMR-Net, specifically designed for photometric measurement tasks in SDSS survey images. The model combines convolutional layers with Self-Attention mechanisms to efficiently extract spatial and channel features, thereby improving the accuracy and robustness of photometric measurements. Experimental results show that CSMR-Net surpasses traditional methods in both accuracy and computational speed, demonstrating its superior performance in processing large-scale astronomical datasets.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Apriori Method on Shapley Features
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: The Fuzzy Apriori Method (FAM) is a typical data mining tool with strong uncertainty-handling capability. However, the assumption of equal contribution of each feature is hampering its running speed and leverage of post-hoc interpretability provided by Shapley values. In this study, we improve the F AM by ranking features through their Shapley values. Each feature's contribution can be used to explain the features and the prior interpretability of feature selection. We term such a FAM as Shapley-FAM (S-FAM). The concept behind S-FAM is to compute the Shapley value for each feature before determining the fuzzy membership in the FAM. Subsequently, it identifies features with higher contributions, generates frequent itemsets and association rules and ultimately applies these rules to classify the 10 selected UCI benchmark datasets. With its simple principle, S-FAM keeps at least comparable to and even better than F AM in the sense of testing classification accuracy, rule count, and computational complexity on most of all the adopted datasets.

articleTitle: Multiple Access Scheme for End Spreading Using Dynamic Codebook
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Since widespread use of the internet, network security has been one of the key concerns for people. End spreading from end hopping that is active defense technologies. But it has a weakness that only support two user to communicate. In this paper, a new network communication strategy is proposed to solve the weakness. It combines the end spreading with idea of codebook. The strategy can change of end information on both sides of communication by using the end spreading technology. And it use code book to encode and discrete series to as sign of identity. During communication, system closes all ports in firewall. It improves security by using codebook and changing parameter of codebook. Theoretical analysis and experimental results show that our scheme can improve the concealment, security. etc.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence Algorithm with Geological Constraints Establishes Element Porosity Relationship
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: This article focuses on the application of artificial intelligence algorithms with geological constraints to establish a high-precision relationship model between geological elements and porosity. This algorithm integrates geological theory and artificial intelligence techniques, incorporating geological constraints into data analysis and model construction. The predicted porosity obtained through this multiple regression model fits well with the measured porosity, and the geological interpretation is reasonable and consistent with reservoir characteristics. Overall, it is believed that artificial intelligence algorithms with geological constraints can accurately predict the size of reservoir porosity, especially in the study of low resistance reservoir performance, which has certain advantages. This innovative method not only improves the efficiency of geological data analysis but also ensures the geological rationality and practical application value of research results, which has certain significance for promoting the intelligent development of oil and gas exploration and development.

articleTitle: Sparse Sylvester Equation Via Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Numerous solutions have been investigated or ap-plied for both the Sylvester equation and the sparse Sylvester equation. In this paper, we employ the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) to solve the sparse Sylvester equation, while imposing the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$l_{0}$</tex> norm to the original Sylvester equation formulation. We analyze the iteration scheme for updating each variable and present a corresponding algorithm by extending the classical ADMM. Additionally, several numerical experiments are conducted to validate its feasibility and efficiency.

articleTitle: An Implicit Smoothing-enabled Algorithm for Strongly Convex Stochastic Multiobjective Optimization with Equilibrium Constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Stochastic multiobjective optimization has at-tract widespread attention in real-world scenarios. However, the current work mainly focuses on the gradient-based algorithms and there is a lack of effective methods for gradient-free problems. In this paper, we consider strongly convex stochastic multiobjective optimization problem with equilibrium constraints (SMOPEC) which may not be differ-entiable. By ultilizing a local spherical smoothing approxi-mation framework the zeroth-order method for this problem is presented, and the convergence analysis of the proposed algorithm is also provided under adequate assumptions. Finally, numerical experiment is conducted to verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Tracking Moving Targets by Earth Observation Satellites: A Multi-Objective Scheduling Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Tracking moving targets using Earth observation satellites stands as a crucial task. It involves frequent obser-vation of these moving targets to prevent loss and to gather detailed information over extended durations. This necessitates two primary objectives: maximizing observation times and ex-tending observation duration. However, there has been limited simultaneous optimization of these objectives in previous studies. In this research, we utilized decomposition-based multi-objective evolutionary algorithms (MOEAs) to optimize this task model. Recognizing the presence of discrete variables (i.e., discrete design variables), we enhanced a well-established decomposition-based MOEA (MOEA/D) specifically for this challenge. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method in optimizing this task model. It generates a diverse and well-converged set of solutions, providing decision-makers with a range of options to consider.

articleTitle: Finite-time Synchronization of Delayed Inertial Neural Networks via Intermittent Control
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: This paper introduces the inertial neural network model with time-delays at first. Through reduced-order approach, the second-order neural networks can be transformed into two first-order differential equations, which simplify the models. Then, by designing the periodically intermittent control strategy, some algebraic conditions for the finite-time synchronization of delayed inertial neural networks are derived by virtue of finite time stability theorems and inequality techniques. What's more, the constructed controller here is independent with delays. Compared with delay-dependent controller, the controller herein is more suitable for practical applications. Moreover, the settling time of delayed inertial neural networks is estimated. In addition, a numerical example is given to verify the effectiveness of the criteria.

articleTitle: Fixed-Time Zero-Gradient-Sum Algorithm for Disturbed Linear Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Achieving more precise modeling and control of vehicle dynamics for multi-vehicle collaboration is pivotal in steering vehicles toward cleaner, smarter, and safer de-velopment. This paper proposes a novel zero-gradient-sum algorithm (ZGSA) based on disturbed linear heterogeneous multi-agent systems (MASs) to solve distributed optimization problems. Using integral sliding manifold and fixed-time control theory, the designed ZGSA is proven to obtain the exact optimal solution within a fixed time. Moreover, it circumvents the requirement on initial conditions, which is a common constraint in classical ZGSAs. Finally, a simulation substantiates the efficacy and robustness of the designed ZGSA.

articleTitle: A Novel Smoothing Framework for Interval-zero-order Takagi-Sugeno Fuzzy Neural Networks: Combining Interval Analysis with Zero-order TS Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: This study introduces a smoothing interval zero-order Takagi-Sugeno (SI-TS0) fuzzy neural network, a novel approach that combines interval numbers with the zero-order Takagi-Sugeno (TS0) fuzzy neural network. During experimentation, the interval TS0(I-TS0) fuzzy neural net-work led to significant oscillations in the gradient norm of the error function, primarily due to the non-differentiability of the absolute value function. To resolve this problem, a smoothing function was incorporated, successfully mitigating the oscillations and resulting in a more stable and accurate model. Extensive numerical simulations validate the SI-TS0 fuzzy neural network's effectiveness, demonstrating enhanced noise-handling capabilities and robustness, making it a valuable tool for processing fuzzy data in complex systems.

articleTitle: An Expensive Multi-Objective Evolutionary Algorithm with RBF-IDW Surrogate Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: In surrogate-assisted multi-objective evolutionary optimization, surrogate models provide approximations for each solution on each objective, with varying quality. In the proposed algorithm, the RBF-IDW surrogate model replaces the Gaussian process model used in the original algorithm, constructing a model for each objective function and identifying candidate solutions during the optimization phase. A Gaussian process model is then used to approximate performance indicators measuring convergence and diversity. Finally, the solution with the maximum expected improvement is selected and evaluated using the expensive objective function. The algorithm's feasibility is demonstrated through tests on the DTLZ and WFG suites.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Spatial Resolution of Galaxy Images Using an Advanced Conditional Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: High-resolution images of galaxies can reveal more galaxy features. However, due to the optical performance limitations of telescopes, there are significant differences in the resolution and sharpness of galaxy images obtained by different telescopes. Therefore, high-resolution galaxy images are reconstructed by mapping low-resolution images into the high-resolution image domain through image processing techniques without changing the existing telescope equipment. In this paper, we propose an advanced conditional denoising diffusion probabilistic model, GalaxSR3, which is an optimized version of the SR3 model for reconstructing galaxy images. We constructed and trained low and high-resolution datasets using the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) and Dark Energy Spectroscopic Sky Survey (DESI). Experimental results demonstrate that GalaxSR3 achieves a Peak Signal to Noise Ratio (PSNR) of 30.77 dB and a Learned Perceptual Image Patch Similarity (LPIPS) value of 0.05, outperforming mainstream models such as SRGAN, EDSR, and HAT. The reconstructed images using the GalaxSR3 model can significantly improve the resolution, enhance the boundary contrast between the cantilever and the nucleus of galaxies, and accurately reconstruct the details of galaxies.

articleTitle: Enhancing Object Detection in Swin Transformer via Global Focusing Mechanism and Data Diversification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: The Tiny-ImageN et dataset challenges object detection due to variable object sizes, complex backgrounds, and imbalanced data, which existing Swin Transformer models fail to address adequately. This paper proposes an object detection algorithm that integrates a global focusing mechanism with a data diversification strategy. The global focusing mechanism enhances the model's ability to detect objects of various sizes, while data diversification, through techniques like rotation, clipping, and scaling, improves generalization and reduces overfitting. Experiments on Tiny-ImageNet show the promising performance compared with the state-of-the-arts methods through offering innovative solutions to persistent object detection challenges.

articleTitle: Identification of Rock Cracks in Outcrop Areas Based on Improved DeepLab V3+
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: The study of reservoir fractures has always been a key focus in oil and gas exploration and development, and the most intuitive method is to observe rock fractures in outcrop areas. Manual surveying has low efficiency and strong subjectivity, so identifying rock fractures in outcrop areas has always been a difficult task. In response to this difficulty, this article utilizes drone oblique photography technology to significantly improve surveying efficiency, and proposes an improved DeepLabv3+ semantic segmentation model to achieve accurate segmentation of rock fractures. The experimental results showed that the MAP (Mean Average Precision) of the improved DeepLabv3+ model reached 83.77%, which was 12.44% higher than the original DeepLabv3+ model; MIoU (Mean Intersection over Union) has increased from 68.21 % to 78.84%; The accuracy has increased from 74.83% to 91.66%; The parameter count is only 15.14M. The experimental results show that the improved DeepLabv3+ model in this paper exhibits superior segmentation performance in rock fracture segmentation tasks in field outcrop areas, and has good mobile deployment performance.

articleTitle: Multi-Frame Super-Resolution Phase Retrieval Based on Consensus Equalization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Super-resolution phase retrieval refers to the reconstruction of high-resolution images from amplitude information, which plays a crucial role in the field of image processing. This paper proposes a multi-frame super-resolution phase retrieval algorithm based on consensus equalization, which balances the data fidelity term of the super-resolution phase retrieval with the TV denoising term. The TV denoising algorithm is combined with the traditional projection algorithm. This paper also tests the proposed algorithm in simulation data and evaluates the algorithm for the case at different Gaussian noise levels and different frames, where it is proved that the consensus equalization outperforms other algorithms with strong image reconstruction capability.

articleTitle: Tomato Leaf Detection Algorithm Based on Improved YOLOv5
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: To address the challenges of complex backgrounds and low accuracy in detecting tomato leaves, we propose an improved tomato leaf detection model, YOLOv5s-SPD, based on the YOLOv5 network, for identifying tomato leaf diseases. First, the SSConv module is introduced into the backbone network of the YOLOv5 algorithm, replacing the C3 module with the SSConv module to reduce feature redundancy in both spatial and channel dimensions, thus lowering the computational load of the model. Additionally, a PSA attention mechanism is incorporated to enhance the model's feature extraction capability for tomato leaf boundaries in harsh environments, reducing the miss detection rate. The bounding box loss function is also replaced with DIoU, taking into account the distance and overlap between bounding boxes, thereby enabling more precise measurement of detection box accuracy and improving the positioning accuracy of tomato leaves. Experimental results show that compared to the original YOLOv5 algorithm, the improved algorithm increases the mean precision by 2.4%, reaching 85.9%. The recall rate also shows a significant improvement.

articleTitle: A Lightweight Model for Human-Object Interaction Recognition in Underground Coal Mines Based on Instance Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Existing behavior recognition methods for underground coal mines(UCM) are often limited to single scenarios, typically focusing on detecting and warning of specific abnormal behaviors, such as the hazardous action of crossing conveyor belts. However, miners working underground for extended periods engage in a variety of actions and operations, which are closely linked to the environment and the objects they interact with. Fine-grained recognition of these behaviors is essential for enhancing intelligent monitoring capabilities and improving safety in coal production. To address this, we propose a lightweight recognition model for human-object interaction (HOI) behavior in UCM based on instance segmentation. The model simultaneously monitors miners and relevant objects, using an instance segmentation network to capture the location and shape information of both humans and objects. By integrating this information and applying rule-based reasoning, the model achieves accurate and fine-grained recognition of miners' behaviors. Experimental results show that the proposed model reaches a new level of accuracy in detecting miners, objects, and behavior recognition, with model parameters of only 2.3M and an inference speed of 120 fps, demonstrating superior efficiency and scalability. This model significantly enhances intelligent monitoring in UCM and improves overall safety and productivity.

articleTitle: CNN-LSTM Low-Resistivity Reservoir Fluid Identification Method Based on Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Low-resistivity reservoirs are becoming increasingly significant in oil and gas exploration due to their extensive distribution and substantial reserves. However, their complex characteristics often render traditional logging interpretations insufficient. This study focuses on the low-resistivity reservoir fluids of the Hanjiang Formation and Zhujiang Formation in the Enping Sag of the Pearl River Mouth Basin. By analyzing gas logging data, quantitative fluorescence, and geochemical logging from 32 wells in the study area, we propose a hybrid model. This model combines the strengths of the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory Network (LSTM) and integrates an attention mechanism to enhance its ability to process small sample sizes of low-resistivity reservoir fluids, thereby improving recognition accuracy. The research findings show that the hybrid model significantly outperforms traditional single models in identifying low-resistivity reservoirs, achieving an accuracy rate of 88.43%, which surpasses single model performances by 2% to 8%. These results not only enhance the predictive accuracy of the model but also establish a new technical approach for identifying low-resistivity reservoirs.

articleTitle: Integral Reinforcement Reciprocal Zhang Neural Net for Time-Varying Linear Equations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Solving time-varying linear equations is a com-mon challenge encountered in engineering and science. The development of neural dynamic systems has led to the creation of various feedback neural nets that effectively solve continuous time-varying linear equations. In this context, reciprocal Zhang neural net (RZNN) was developed, which is focused by this work, providing an explicit inverse-free continuous model for solving time-varying linear equations. However, the continuous model often struggle with noise interference, e.g., Gaussian noise, during the solving process. This paper enhances RZNN model with an integral reinforcement term to improve robustness of the explicit continuous models with noisy conditions. Furthermore, we optimize the RZNN solving process, making it easier for implementation in circuit systems and numerical simulations.

articleTitle: A Multi-Label Prediction Model for Iron Ore Sintering Process Incorporating Time Features
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: The steelmaking sintering process is critical for quality control and efficiency in iron production. Addressing the challenge of accurately predicting quality indicators amidst diverse parameters and multiple time scales is essential. In this paper, a multilabel regression model incorporating temporal features is proposed for predicting quality metrics during the sintering process. The model integrates 34 input parameters to predict 7 quality indicators, reflecting the complex nature of the process. By applying the model to real data from a steel plant's No. 2 sintering machine and validating its performance, the study demonstrates the model's effectiveness in multi-label regression tasks. The experimental results show that the model incorporating temporal features performs better in predicting sinter ore quality indicators, effectively capturing complex parameter relationships and providing reliable predictions.

articleTitle: A Novel Path Planning Approach for USV Based on Optimization and Motion Modulation Obstacle Avoidance
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Effective path planning and obstacle avoidance control are essential for ensuring the safe and efficient operation of Unmanned Surface Vehicle (USV) during maritime operations. This paper proposes a Particle Swarm Optimization-based Energy-Efficient Motion Modulation Obstacle Avoidance algorithm (PSOEMMOA) tailored for USV path planning. Considering the kinematic and dynamic characteristics of USV, the PSO algorithm is employed to globally optimize the navigation path, ensuring the USV can maintain optimal navigation performance during obstacle avoidance and the global optimality of the path. Additionally, a novel obstacle avoidance strategy based on motion modulation is designed. This strategy locally adjusts the navigation path of USV according to environmental information, facilitating effective obstacle avoidance. Through simulation experiments, the effectiveness of using PSOEMOOA for path planning in complex environments has been validated.

articleTitle: Efficient Air Defense Temporal Decision-Making Methods Under Unstable Dimensional States
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: To address the needs of future intelligent war-fare, this paper proposes a hierarchical intelligent decision-making algorithm (ATT-PPO) based on the PPO algorithm and multi-head attention mechanism, designed to solve air defense sequential decision-making problems under unsta-ble dimensional states. Traditional reinforcement learning struggles to handle variable-dimensional observation information, whereas ATT-PPO uses the attention mechanism to map variable-dimensional observations into fixed dimensions, thereby enhancing the representation of high-dimensional dynamic data. However, high-dimensional decision spaces increase the learning burden of the algorithm. To mitigate this, a hierarchical reinforcement learning architecture is designed, incorporating domain knowledge to narrow the exploration space and improve decision-making efficiency. Simulation results show that ATT-PPO significantly out-performs traditional expert control methods in cumulative rewards, validating its superior performance.

articleTitle: Uncertainty Quantification of Stochastic Partial Differential Equations Based on Bayesian Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Stochastic Partial Differential Equations (SPDEs) are extensively applied across a multitude of real-world contexts, particularly within the realms of engineering and finance. Given that the input parameters for SPDEs are inherently stochastic, ensuring reliable and robust predictions for the physical systems in question necessitates rigorous uncertainty quantification (UQ). Recently, a multitude of approaches utilizing neural networks to solve SPDEs have emerged, showcasing promising results. However, the majority of these methods operate under the presumption of precisely known parameters. In practical applications, information about parameters can only be obtained through a limited number of sensors. Therefore, we have combined the variational form of SPDEs with Bayesian Neural Networks (BNN) to quantify uncertainties in SPDEs. This approach circumvents the need for second-order derivative calculations, significantly enhancing the accuracy of UQ through the direct application of BNN. Specifically, we employ BNN to model the solution of the SPDE, integrating the governing equations into the likelihood function via automatic differentiation, and employing the Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) technique to draw samples from the posterior distribution. Numerical experiments indicate that our approach substantially enhances the accuracy of UQ for SPDEs.

articleTitle: Chiplet Placement Based on Simulated Annealing with Multi-Precision Thermal Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: With the advent of the post-Moore era, chiplet gains more and more attention. Due to the compact package of multi-chip system, it is necessary to perform chip let placement with consideration of thermal optimization. To alleviate the problem of heavy complexity, the idea of multi- precision simulation is introduced, and we propose a thermal placement algorithm based on simulated annealing algorithm with assistance of multi-precision thermal simulation. Numerical results demonstrate that it can reduce the peak operating temperature of the whole chip let-based system while optimizing the total wirelength. Furthermore, the significant reduction of running time suggests its potential application in the agile development of multi-chip system.

articleTitle: HENet: A Height Estimation Network for Estimating the Height of Buildings from Single Optical Image
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Estimating building height from a single optical (RGB) image is a significant task with applications in urban planning and resource management. Recent advances in deep learning have shown great potential in this domain. In this paper, we propose a deep learning network named HENet, designed to estimate the height of buildings using a classification-regression paradigm. Specifically, we first employ the Visual Geometry Group (VGG16) to extract high-dimensional semantic features. These features are then fused through skip connections between the encoder and decoder. To enhance global information, we incorporate an attention mechanism within the decoder, addressing the local attention limitation of convolutional layers. The decoder generates a rough height map, refined by our proposed segmentation based Adabins (SAdabins), following the classification-regression paradigm to obtain a fine-grained result. Remote sensing images often contain extensive background, leading to a long-tailed distribution of low-height pixels and resulting in underestimated height values. To address this, we introduce the Segment Anything (SAM) to obtain segmentation maps that filter out background in SAdabins. Experiments show that HENet outperforms other baselines in visualization quality and Quantitative evaluations.

articleTitle: GFPN-YOLOv8m: A Deep Learning Network for Astronomical Source Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: In astronomical image processing, issues such as varying target source sizes, partial overlap between sources, and confusion between some sources and the background often cause a decrease in detection accuracy. To cope with these issues, this paper proposed an improved GFPN-YOLOv8m network. Specifically, Coordinate Attention is introduced into the backbone network, embedding positional data into the attention map to achieve more precise target localization and recognition. The Global Feature Pyramid Network (GFPN) is integrated into the neck network to fuse multi-scale features more efficiently. Moreover, an additional layer dedicated to detecting small objects has been incorporated into the detection head, enhancing the ability to detect small objects. Comprehensive experimental results reveal that the proposed network surpasses existing alternatives, achieving an accuracy of 0.984, a recall of 0.971, a mAP50 of 0.993, and a mAP50-95 of 0.779. Therefore, the improved GFPN-YOLOv8m network exhibits higher accuracy and robustness, providing astronomers with more detailed and comprehensive data.

articleTitle: A Study on Skin Lesions Classification Based on Improved EfficientN etB0 Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Skin cancer is the most common type of cancer, and early detection and treatment of skin lesions can greatly improve the cure rate of skin cancer. However, existing skin disease assisted classification networks have some problems such as large number of parameters and complex operations, which are not convenient for deployment on mobile devices. This paper proposes a lightweight convolution neural network method for skin lesion classification. The method replaces the standard convolution module in the first stage of the network based on the lightweight EfficientN etBO with the Ghost module, and adds the CBAM module between the 1 *1 convolution layer and the pooling layer in the ninth stage, to form an improved EfficientNetBO network model. The accuracy of the improved EfficientN etBO on the ISIC2018 skin disease dataset HAMI0000 is 89.38%, the Macro_P, Macro_R, Fl-Score is 0.88, 0.86, 0.87 respectively. The number of parameters is only 5.19M, while the single inference time is 71ms. All of these indicators make the model suitable for deploying skin disease classification models on mobile devices to assist clinical diagnosis.

articleTitle: Semi-Supervised Classification Module for Hyperspectral Images Based on Dual-Stream Attention and Kernel Density Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Deep Neural Networks (DNN) are widely used in hyperspectral image (HSI) classification due to their powerful ability to extract spatial-spectral features. However, the scarcity of labeled samples limits the performance of DNNs. In this paper, an HSI pseudo-sample generation module based on dual-stream attention and kernel density estimation (KDE) is proposed, which enhances the robustness and generalization ability of DNNs by generating and feeding a sufficient number of high-fidelity samples into the network. First, a dual-stream spatial-spectral feature extraction network with serial channel and spatial attention is constructed to map the spectral dimensions to a low-dimensional space while reconstructing discriminative features for different classes. Then, KDE is used to perceive the probability density function of the class distribution in the low-dimensional space. Finally, samples with high matching degrees to the class distribution are selected to generate pseudo-samples. More importantly, our proposed module can be embedded into any DNNs to further improve the performances of these models. Extensive experimental results show that the pseudo-samples generated by our module not only effectively alleviate performance fluctuations of the original network but also significantly improve the classification accuracy of the network.

articleTitle: Evolutionary Multitasking Optimization Based Multi-Objective Network Control Principles for Identifying Personalized Drug Targets with Cancer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Multi-objective optimization-based structural network control principles (MONCP) achieved good performance in identifying personalized drug targets.However, the current approaches neglect the fact that for the same personalized gene interaction networks(PGIN), different MONCPs have some similar properties. Therefore, this paper proposes a evolutionary multitasking optimization framework (called DATCMO) which treats different control principles as multiple optimization tasks and allows the exchange of information between tasks on one PGIN for an individual patient. The technical advantage of this method is to establish a respective auxiliary population for each task, and perform knowledge transfer during the evolutionary process for different MONCPs. The experimental results on 112 breast cancer patients data from The Cancer Genome Atlas indicate that, compared to current advance methods, the proposed algorithm proves to be more competitive.

articleTitle: Efficient and Accurate Capsule Networks with B-Spline-Based Activation Functions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: This paper introduces Capsule Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (CapsuleKAN), a novel capsule network architecture. It advances traditional capsule networks by enhancing convolutional and fully connected layers through Conv KAN and Linear-KAN. ConvKAN employs B-spline-based convolutions to generate superior feature maps and higher quality capsules. In contrast, LinearKAN utilizes B-splines as activation functions to capture complex nonlinearities with fewer parameters, optimizing the network's efficiency. Evaluations on the MNIST dataset revealed that CapsuleConvKAN, CapsuleLinearKAN, and CapsuleConv-LinearKAN achieved accuracy rates of 99.72%, 99.71 %, and 99.75%, respectively, with significant parameter reductions of 30K, 1.42M, and 1.44M. On the FashionMNIST dataset, the models attained accuracy rates of 93.22 %, 93.25 %, and 93.34 %, respectively. These results clearly demonstrate that CapsuleKAN models significantly enhance both accuracy and parameter efficiency compared to traditional capsule networks.

articleTitle: Broad Learning System with Coordinate Iterative Training Mode
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Broad learning system (BLS) has emerged as an effective alternative to deep learning. Due to the linear output characteristics of BLS, the generalized inverse method based on ridge regression is commonly used to solve for the hidden layer weights. However, when dealing with large matri-ces, the generalized inverse algorithm often underperforms. Moreover, it considers all features simultaneously during computation, resulting in redundancy and inefficiency. To address these issues, we first extend the RCD algorithm for multi-output problems, enabling parallel computation of multiple systems. Furthermore, the introduction of a novel iterative update strategy allows for the incorporation of randomness while capturing important low-probability feature information, thereby achieving superior results. Thus, we propose an enhanced parallel randomized coordinate de-scent (EPRCD) algorithm for weight calculation. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the newly proposed algorithm performs well on hlah-dimcnsional datasets.

articleTitle: L∞ Time-delay Unknown Input Set-membership Observer-based Actuator Fault Detection for Discrete System with Uncertainties
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: This paper focuses on the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_{\infty}$</tex> time-delay unknown input set-membership observer-based actuator fault detection problem for discrete system. In order to make fault detection robust to uncertainties including unknown interference and modelling errors, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_{\infty}$</tex> performance index is employed in designing the novel observer. Moreover, the observer conditions are converted into an optimization problem constrained by linear matrix inequalities. Under the assumption that uncertainties are unknown but bounded by zonotopes, an actuator fault detection scheme based on accurate residual thresholds estimated by a zonotope set-membership approach is established. Finally, a numerical is provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Robust Distributed Resource Allocation Based on PID Control with Nabla Fractional Difference
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: In many real-world applications, resource allocation in the presence of disturbances poses significant challenges due to the dynamic and uncertain nature of the environment. Traditional optimization algorithms often struggle to maintain robustness and efficiency under these conditions. This paper addresses the resource allocation problem with disturbances by proposing a novel distributed optimization algorithm. The proposed algorithm integrates the principles of proportional- integral-derivative (PID) control, discrete sliding mode control, and nabla fractional difference, resulting in enhanced robustness, flexibility, and efficiency. Through extensive numerical simu-lations, the correctness and effectiveness of the algorithm are thoroughly validated, demonstrating its potential to outperform existing approaches in disturbed environments.

articleTitle: Lithology Identification of Improved Model based on DeepLabv3 + Deep Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Aiming at the complexity of outcrop lithology identification, an improved outcrop lithology identification algorithm based on DeepLabv3 + is proposed. We use the Xception network replaced by the MobileNetV2 module to enhance the ability to extract lithologic features and make the model more lightweight. In order to segment pixels more accurately, the CA (Coordinate attention) attention mechanism is introduced, so that the improved backbone network can extract lithologic features more accurately in complex environments. The experimental results show that compared with the traditional DeepLabv3 +, the accuracy of the improved algorithm is increased by 1.08 percentage points, the MP A is increased by 2.4 percentage points, and the average classification accuracy is 94.86 %. Compared with other mainstream semantic segmentation models, all aspects of performance are more prominent.

articleTitle: Equipment Effectiveness Assessment via Knowledge Graph and Analytic Hierarchy Process
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel equipment effectiveness assessment method based on the knowledge graph and the analytic hierarchy process. In the method, the focused web crawling technology is adopted to select the relevant web pages from Wikipedia and obtain reliable equipment dataset for the construction of knowledge graph. Through data preprocessing and ontology construction, a hierarchical knowledge graph is formed and then the knowledge storage and visualization are implemented in Neo4j. Based on the knowledge graph and the similarity of word vectors, the network layer of the analytic hierarchy process composing of a series of different effectiveness indicators is automatically extracted. Through the determination of the weight vector and the score vector of the indicators to the effectiveness performance, the effectiveness assessment of the equipments is achieved. An illustration example based on the effectiveness assessment comparison between two equipments is finally given to verify the rationality of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Background Extraction Method Based on ESO-LFFDL
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Background extraction is a commonly used method for moving object detection in video sequences. Most background extraction methods rely on specific models to handle complex scenarios in different situations, in which the problem of model distortion always arises. In this paper, a local full form dynamic linearization (LFFDL) method based on an extended state observer (ESO) is proposed to address the above problem in background extraction. The LFFDL method is developed to build the dynamic relationship between background images and original images as a parametric data model, which can be adaptively updated with a parameter estimation law. Meanwhile, an ESO is designed to estimate the uncertainty in background extraction, and the estimation value is used as a compensation to improve the robustness. The simulation results indicate that the proposed method can achieve the background and foreground extraction in different scenarios, and the F-measures and precision reach over 95%, which is better than other existing methods.

articleTitle: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for WEEE Recycling Vehicle Path Planning Based on Graph Attention Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: With the global surge in WEEE generation, optimizing vehicle routing for recycling has become a critical area of research. This paper introduces a MARL method built upon graph attention networks (GAT) to solve the vehicle routing problem in WEEE recycling. By representing recycling sites as graph nodes and vehicles as agents, GAT captures the intricate relationships between them. Coupled with a MARL framework, this approach enhances task efficiency and routing flexibility. Experimental results indicate that the proposed method outperforms static solvers by adapting more effectively to dynamic environments and handling demand fluctuations and complex traffic conditions. Furthermore, it demonstrates greater flexibility and collaboration compared to single-agent reinforcement learning, providing a superior solution for dynamic recycling tasks. This study lays the foundation for further exploration of MARL-GNN integration, with potential applications in waste management and sustainable logistics in smart cities.

articleTitle: Vehicle Routing Model Based on Real- Time Road Conditions Considering Carbon Emissions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: The vehicle routing problem is an important research topic in the field of intelligent transport. The accurate vehicle routing model is the key to solving the vehicle routing problem. With the awakening awareness of low-carbon logistics and the urgent need for sustainable development, carbon emissions have become a focus of attention in vehicle route modelling. Vehicle routing model based on real-time road conditions considering carbon emission (VRM-RCCE) is proposed in this paper to solve the low-carbon intelligent transport. Firstly, the vehicle speed is identified as a key variable that affects carbon emissions by analyzing the carbon emissions mechanisms. The vehicle speed is predicted accurately based on real-time road conditions. Secondly, a vehicle routing model, considering vehicle numbers, the routing length and the carbon emission, is constructed. The carbon emission is calculated through the predicted vehicle speed. Finally, the validity of VRM-RCCE is verified using Gurobi. Optimal routing schemes are obtained using ant colony optimization algorithm. The VRM-RCCE can effectively assist in solving the vehicle routing problem, providing a powerful theoretical support and practical tool for intelligent transport management.

articleTitle: A Photovoltaic Power Generation Prediction Method Combining STL Decomposition and Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: As global demand for renewable energy increases, photovoltaic (PV) power generation has become crucial for grid management and energy optimization. This paper introduces a novel PV power forecasting method that combines Seasonal-Trend Decomposition using LOESS (STL) with a Self-Attention Mechanism (STL-SA). This approach utilizes STL to break down time series data, enhancing the model's capacity to identify intrinsic photovoltaic patterns, while the self-attention mecha-nism focuses on learning long-term dependencies within the time series. Experimental validation on five public datasets shows that the STL-SA method excels in multivariate multi-step forecasting tasks, delivering remarkable results with real photovoltaic data.

Author Keywords: seasonal time series decomposition using loess

articleTitle: Vehicular Lead-Acid Battery Fault Prediction Method based on A-DeepFM
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Vehicle lead-acid battery failures can severely impact automotive safety and normal usage. Early detection of potential faulty batteries has become an important issue in the industry. This paper addresses the complex operating conditions of vehicle lead-acid batteries, the large volume of battery data with few signal dimensions, low efficiency in fault point annotation, and inadequate prediction accuracy. A deep learning-based fault prediction method using multi-dimensional time series data from vehicle lead-acid batteries is proposed. By employing an automatic fault segment annotation method, manual feature design, and an improved A-DeepFM model, the performance of the battery fault prediction task is optimized. Finally, on an independent test set containing 10000 batteries, the results show that the A-DeepFM model achieves a prediction Precision of 93% in the vehicle lead-acid battery prediction task, improving by more than 2.2% compared to expert strategies and model methods and able to predict battery failures on average 5.3 days in advance, indicating a clear advantage of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Enhancing Deep Learning Model Performance by Integrating CBAM and CondConv Technologies
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: In the field of transmission line inspection, accurately identifying the status of insulators is crucial for ensuring the stable operation of the power system. To address the issue of low recognition rates under complex backgrounds associated with traditional methods, this paper proposes an improved model based on the YOLOv8 algorithm, integrating the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) and Conditional Convolution (CondConv) to enhance the detection accuracy and adaptability for transmission line insulators. The CBAM enhances the model's ability to identify specific insulator features by strengthening the representation of key spatial and channel features, while CondConv dynamically adjusts convolutional kernels to optimize the model's response to complex background variations. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared to the traditional YOLOv8 model, this architecture significantly improves the detection accuracy of insulators in varying environments while maintaining real- time processing speed. This research provides robust technical support for the development of automated transmission line inspection technologies.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach for Updating the Penalty Parameter of Alternating Direction Method for the L1-norm Problem
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: An adaptive penalty update criterion for the Altering Direction Method (ADM) for solving L1 problem is presented in this paper. The criterion adjusts penalty parameters based on the primal-dual constraint function value ratios and their relative changes. A dynamic update scheme, with default settings for startup, frequency, and scaling, is developed through iterative analysis. Numerical tests indicate that the new algorithm accelerates traditional ADM and offers more flexibility for initial penalty parameter selection.

articleTitle: CLIP as Auxiliary Supervisor for Weakly Supervised Semantic Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Weakly supervised semantic segmentation (WSSS) with image-level labels effectively alleviates the time-consuming and laborious issue of manually annotating image pixels in semantic segmentation. However, the class activation map (CAM) only highlights the most discriminative regions, resulting in an incomplete pseudo-label, which provides insufficient supervision for training the semantic segmentation network. In recent years, the Contrastive Language Image Pre-Training (CLIP) model has received widespread attention due to its powerful zero-shot learning capability. Based on this, we propose a CLIP as auxiliary supervision framework (CAS) that utilizes CLIP as an auxiliary task to enhance supervision information, providing more accurate pseudo-labels for segmentation training. Specifically, we propose a Auxiliary Mask Generation (AMG) module, which uses CLIP to generate additional auxiliary masks and designs an auxiliary loss to supervise the generation of higher quality segmentation pseudo labels. Moreover, we propose a CAM Fusion Module (CFM), which leverages CLIP's potential for downstream tasks to enhance the localization ability of CAM. To further enhance the supervision provided by CLIP, we propose a Dynamic Mask Noise Filtering module (DNF), introducing Gaussian Mixture Modeling to dynamically reduce the noise in auxiliary masks. Large-scale experiments prove the effectiveness of the proposed CLIP as an auxiliary supervision framework, we validate the reliability of our method on the PASCAL VOC 2012 dataset and demonstrate significant improvements in segmentation performance.

articleTitle: A Bat K-Medoids Clustering Algorithm with Clonal Selection Technique for DNA Microarray Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: In bioinformatics fields, researchers analyze tumors at the molecular level using DNA microarray data, and further classify different tumor subtypes according to the different expressions of related pathogenic genes in the same tumor. High dimensions and small samples is characteristic of DNA microarray data sets. In this paper, we proposed an improved bat clonal K-medoids clustering algorithm (IBACK-medoids). In the IBACK-medoids, we improved standard bat algorithm through accelerating the convergence speed. Furthermore, we introduce the main idea of clonal selection algorithm in the improved bat algorithm. Finally, to obtain more better clustering convergence, the improved bat clonal algorithm and K-medoids algorithm are combined. In experiments, the evaluation tools for clustering algorithms are F -measure, Entropy and Purity. The experimental results show the effectiveness of our proposed algorithms.

articleTitle: Neighbor Interaction Aware Graph Neural Network for Collaborative Filtering
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Recently, recommendation algorithms based on Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have demonstrated robust capabilities in learning representations of users and items. However, these methods often rely on aggregation functions like sum/mean/max pooling operations to form user and item representations, overlooking the importance of interaction information between neighboring nodes for node representation. To address these limitations, this paper introduces the Neighbor Interactions Aware Graph Neural Network (NIA-GNN) method for collaborative filtering. This approach explicitly models both the aggregation and interaction information of neighboring nodes, capturing relationship information between adjacent nodes to enhance user and item representations, improve recommendation effectiveness, and boost the model's predictive power. We perform extensive experiments on two real datasets to confirm that NIA-GNN significantly enhances recommendation performance. Further analysis underscores the significance of neighbor interaction information in refining user and item representations, validating the rationale and efficacy of the NIA-GNN method.

articleTitle: Multiobjective Multitask Evolutionary Optimization based on M2M Decomposition with Dynamic Resource Allocation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Multiobjective multitask optimization (MO-MTO) algorithms aim to solve a set of multiobjective optimization problems (MOPs) simultaneously in a single run. This paper proposed an innovative MO-MTO algorithm based on M2M decomposition and dynamic resource allocation (MMTOID-DRA) for the first time. In this algorithm, each task in an MO-MTO problem is decomposed into a series of constrained multiobjective subproblems to ensure population diversity. Furthermore, during the iteration process, more computational resources are dynamically allocated to promising subregions to accelerate convergence. MMTO/D-DRA was comprehensively tested on nine benchmark problems. The experimental results compared it with five state-of-the-art MO-MTO algorithms, demonstrating the superiority of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Microseismic Data Augmentation Based on Improved Generative Adversarial Network and Policy Gradient
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Microseismic data plays a crucial role in seismic exploration and oil/gas exploitation. However, its high acquisition cost leads to scarcity, making effective augmentation of microseis-mic datasets a critical issue. In this paper, a new approach based on policy gradient and generative adversarial network (GAN) is proposed, which aims to improve the scale and variety of micro-seismic data sets. We integrate GANs with policy gradient algorithms, employing a tailored policy network to better capture the distribution characteristics of microseismic data. Through adversarial training, the generator network continually refines synthesized microseismic data, while the discriminator network assesses the authenticity of generated samples. This adversarial approach effectively enhances the quality of generated data, aligning it more closely with the distribution characteristics of real microseismic data. Incorporating self-attention mechanisms within the generator facilitates improved learning of long-term temporal features in microseismic signals, thereby generating synthetic samples that closely resemble real micro-seismic signals. Experimental validation on real microseismic datasets demonstrates that the proposed method based on policy gradient and GANs effectively augments microseismic datasets. The synthesized data exhibits statistical properties and geological significance comparable to real data, providing richer and more diverse data resources for subsequent geological analysis and exploration efforts.

articleTitle: A Novel Weight Initialization Method for Neural Networks with Nonlinear Output
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a weight initialization method to address the challenges associated with initializing models that utilize the softmax function to convert their final output into probabilities. Utilizing the first-order Taylor expansion, we approximate the model's nonlinear output with a linear function, which enables us to fine-tune the weights of the last layer by minimizing the initial loss function. For the other layers, we apply the well-established Kaiming initialization technique to ensure that the variance of the output is equal to the variance of the input, ensuring a more stable training process. This strategic optimization yields weights that are close to optimal, thereby accelerating the convergence rate and enhancing the efficiency of the training process. Experiments comparing our method against four traditional initialization methods, showing our approach has a significant advantage, especially during the initial training phase, while remaining competitive in the later stages of training.

articleTitle: Short-Term Tariff Prediction for High Penetration New Energy Electricity Market Based on Singular Spectrum Analysis and CNN-GRU Combination Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Accurate electricity price forecasts are essential for electricity market participants to make informed choices. The complexity of forecasting electricity prices continues to rise in new power systems that consist mainly of new energy generation. In order to improve the accuracy of electricity price prediction in power markets with a high proportion of new energy sources, this paper proposes an electricity price prediction technique based on singular spectrum analysis after combing the existing electricity price prediction techniques. In this paper, a short-term electricity market price prediction model combining Singular Spectrum Analysis (SSA), Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) is constructed. The method takes electricity price, load and new energy generation as input, decomposes and reconstructs the original data by using SSA, and constructs CNN architecture consisting of convolution layer and pooling layer for trend component and oscillation component of each array, respectively, to extract high-dimensional features reflecting complex dynamic changes of electricity price. The feature vectors proposed are constructed in the form of time series, which are used as inputs to the GRU network, and the internal dynamics of the features are modelled and learnt as a rule. Eventually, the final electricity price prediction results were obtained by accumulating the prediction sequences. The experimental results confirm that this method can significantly improve the accuracy of short-term electricity price prediction.

articleTitle: Density Functional Theory Calculation of Hydrogen Adsorption on Metal-Doped WO3 Monolayer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Hydrogen-sensitive nanomaterials were important to construct hydrogen sensors for preventing fire or explosion caused by hydrogen leakage.
