In this paper, density functional theory (DFT) is used to study the calculation of Pt-, Pd-, Ni-, Ir-modified cubic phase tungsten trioxide (WO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>), and the adsorption and desorption characteristics of hydrogen gas are studied by analyzing its state density, adsorption energy, charge transfer amount and other properties. The DFT investigation results show that the Pt- WO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and Pd- WO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> greatly improved the sensitivity toward hydrogen, which demonstrated good characteristics of adsorption and desorption for hydrogen gas. The Pt- WO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and Pd-WO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> have great potential for applications in constructing high-performance hydrogen sensors. This work provided a foundation for the material design and sensing mechanism interpretation.

articleTitle: A Multi-Stage Deep Learning Approach for Stellar Mass Prediction of Galaxies
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: In astronomical research, the stellar mass of galaxies is a crucial physical parameter that directly influences a galaxy's luminosity, dynamical properties, and evolutionary process. Tra-ditional methods for calculating stellar mass rely on spectral data, which require complex techniques to obtain and limit their broader application. With advancements in astronomical observation technology and deep learning, it has become possible to estimate galaxy parameters from photometric images using deep learning. This paper proposes a multi-band deep learning approach, integrating the improved Rep Vit framework with the CBAM attention mechanism and a lightweight Stem module, and designing a new Head module. We introduce the Stellar Mass Prediction Network, Multi-Stage Attention-Enhanced Convolutional Network (MACNet), which effectively captures complex features in galaxy images. Experimental results validate the superior performance of this method for stellar mass prediction, demonstrating that the proposed approach outperforms existing methods and provides new possibilities for predicting galaxy parameters.

articleTitle: ATSCOT: Chain of Thought for Structuring Anesthesia Medical Records
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: This study proposes a method called ATSCOT (Anesthesia Text Structuring Chain of Thought), aimed at leveraging the powerful capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) to structure anesthesia medical records. The ATSCOT method enhances the semantic understanding abilities of Large Language Models through carefully designed prompts, breaking down complex anesthesia text processing tasks into several key steps. This Chain of Thought approach helps the model better understand and organize intricate medical records. The study constructed a specialized test set containing 100 anesthesia-related medical records and employed a combination of automatic evaluation, human assessment, and GPT-4 evaluation to comprehensively assess the model's performance. Evaluation criteria include the accuracy of information extraction, contextual understanding, and reasoning abilities. Experimental results indicate that the ATSCOT method performs excellently in structuring anesthesia texts, showing significant improvements compared to baseline methods. The findings suggest that the proposed approach has the potential to greatly assist in the efficient and accurate processing of anesthesia medical records, ultimately benefiting patient care and clinical decision-making.

articleTitle: Adaptive Fractional-Order PID Controller Design and Parameter Tuning for Vehicle Longitudinal Control
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: To enhance traffic efficiency and ensure passenger comfort, an Adaptive Fractional-Order PID (AFOPID) controller is proposed for longitudinal control in automated vehicles. Initially, the traditional PID controller is improved by incorporating fractional-order calculus, enhancing the overall control performance. The gain parameters of the fractional-order PID controller are updated using the gradient descent method according to sliding mode surfaces to further enhance the robustness of the control system. To ensure accurate tuning of controller parameters, a hybrid strategy is employed to improve the Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO). Simulation results indicate that the hybrid strategy-enhanced grey wolf optimizer exhibits faster convergence in the early stages and superior global search capabilities. Additionally, the proposed AFOPID controller exhibits reduced control output fluctuations and achieves higher average speeds, and more gentle speed changes in car-following scenarios. Multi-vehicle platoon experiments further confirm the controller's robust queue stability.

articleTitle: Research on Speech Playback Spoof Detection Based on ASV Spoof 2021
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Speech playback spoofing refers to the use of pre-recorded and authenticated speech of the target speaker, through some playback devices to play the recorded speech and send it to the ASV system. As a result, the error acceptance rate of ASV system is significantly increased. Based on this, this paper designs a speech playback spoofing detection system model based on deep neural network to distinguish real audio from replayed audio. Reduce the error acceptance rate of ASV systems. To be specific, firstly, the audio features of the original speech are extracted by the convolutional neural network and combined with the MFCC features. Then a speech playback detection model is designed based on the cyclic neural network and a speech playback detection system model is built. Experimental results show that, compared with the existing algorithms, The voice playback spoofing detection system based on ASV spoof 2021 can well distinguish real voice from replayed voice and effectively avoid replayed voice from entering the ASV system.

articleTitle: Multi-Element Features Extraction from High Spatial Resolution Remote Sensing Image Based on Semantic Segmentation Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: The high spatial resolution remote sensing image contains rich special information with a great detail. Traditional segmentation methods have low classification accuracy, the complexity of high spatial resolution remote sensing images also requires higher the classification technology of remote sensing images. In recent years, neural networks have made remarkable achievements in the field of image segmentation. Our method was tested on the High-Resolution Remote Sensing Segmentation Dataset, comparative semantic segmentation models such as FCN (Fully Convolutional Networks), SegNet and DeepLab-V3+. Experimental results showed that the overall accuracy of FCN, SegNet and DeepLab-V3+ methods were 82.8%, 85.5% and 87.4 %. The analysis results show that the DeepLab-V3+algorithm has higher iterative efficiency in model training; SegNet is the second, and the FCN algorithm has the worst iterative efficiency. The DeepLab-V3+algorithm has the highest accuracy and the fastest iteration efficiency in the extraction of multi-element features from high spatial resolution remote sensing images, which achieved a balance between accuracy and computational resource consumption.

articleTitle: Operational Behavior Computing: Task Assignment Optimization Considering Worker Behavior and Algorithmic Responsibility
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: This study addresses a task assignment optimization problem by accounting for the heterogeneity of employee behavior and the accountability of algorithm deployment. Initially, we explore the variability within picker behavior across multiple dimensions, with experiments indicating notable differences. These behavioral variabilities are then integrated into a fairness-constrained task assignment model, aiming to minimize the maximum task completion time. The model's predictive accuracy is confirmed through some machine learning algorithms. A comparative analysis of various algorithms, including Variable Neighborhood Search (VNS), Adaptive Large Neighborhood Search (ALNS), Harmony Search (HS), Artificial Bee Colony (ABC), and Genetic Algorithm (GA), indicates that VNS and ALNS provide enhanced interpretability and timeliness, which are crucial for real-world scenarios demanding rapid response times, such as those in the second or millisecond range.

articleTitle: Reverse Osmosis Water System Based on Sparrow Search Improved Active Disturbance Rejection Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: In this paper, a reverse osmosis water making system is designed to solve the problem that the conductivity of produced water is unstable due to the change in ambient temperature and the fluctuation of water quality. A unique double pump double film double stage reverse osmosis process was designed and the active disturbance rejection controller was introduced to realize the effective combination of booster pump and reverse osmosis membrane. Aiming at the problems of high complexity, long time, and expe-rience dependence in the process of controller parameter adjustment, the sparrow search algorithm is used to realize automatic parameter optimization. Through the simulation of the system, the results show that the reverse osmosis water system shows good adaptability and anti-interference performance in dealing with external interference.

articleTitle: Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Wind Turbine Rotating Machinery Based on Dilated Inception Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: In the wind power sector, remaining useful life (RUL) predictions guarantee the reliable and safe operation of rotating machinery. Traditional deep learning models have a complex and fixed structure, which makes it difficult to extract effective information features from bearing degradation patterns. In this paper, a novel RUL prediction method named dilated inception network (DiIncepN et) is proposed. In the proposed DiIncepNet, signals reconstructed by the denoising autoencoder (DAE) are used as input. Dilated convolution and adaptive pooling operations are introduced in Inception v2 to build the DiIncep module. This improvement increases the receptive field based on capturing features at multiple scales and eliminates the need to manually adjust pooling parameters. The stacked DiIncep modules subsequently integrate (bidirectional gated recurrent unit) BiGRU and Dropout layers. This facilitates the network to capture temporal dependencies and destroys weight co-adaptation. Experimental results on the XJTU-SY datasets show that the network is able to accurately predict the RUL with superior generalization ability and robustness.

articleTitle: MSCA-UNet: Multi-Scale Channel Adaptive Sensing Module for Medical Image Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Recent advancements in CNNs for medical image segmentation have focused on the combination of CNN and Transformer architectures to capture both local and global features. However, challenges remain, such as effectively utilizing fused features at the encoder-decoder bottleneck and addressing blurred object edges in datasets. To tackle these issues, we introduce a multi-scale channel adaptive sensing module, enhancing the model's representational and perceptual capabilities by integrating multi-scale and channel-specific information. Additionally, we propose a cross-perception module and multi-scale segmentation head to improve global coordination and multi-scale information gathering. Experiments on the ACDC and Synapse datasets demonstrate our model's superiority.

articleTitle: AdanB: Adan with Dynamic Bound for Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: The adaptive Nesterov Momentum Algorithm (Adan) is a recently proposed efficient adaptive optimization algorithm that innovatively combines the Adam algorithm with an improved version of the NAG method to produce superior performance. However, Adan still suffers from unstable learning rates near convergence due to the second-order moments. To this end, this paper proposes a modified Adan with dynamic bound (AdanB) by employing a clipping trick. AdanB achieves a smooth transition from Adan to SGD by introducing dynamic learning rate boundaries, thereby improving the model's generalization ability while maintaining high learning speed. Extensive simulations are conducted to confirm the superiority of AdanB over Adan when training three popular neural models on two benchmark image classification problems.

articleTitle: Calibration of Fractional-order Car-following Model Using Improved Whale Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Intelligent driver model (IDM) is a famous car-following model in the traffic flow theory to illustrate the traffic phenomenon. While fractional-order calculus can precisely depict and predict various complex phenomena with the memory effect and nonlinear characteristics. Thus, this paper creatively proposes a fractional-order intelligent driver model (FIDM). Besides, to calibrate the model more accurately, we innovatively put forward a novel improved whale optimization algorithm, named as WOAFSC, fused with fractional-order strategy and stochastic center search strategy. Finally, the proposed FIDM and WOAFSC are validated on three data sets separately. Experimental results demonstrate their stronger robustness and higher accuracy. It should be noted that this research can provide theoretical support and practical guidance for fractional-order calculus in the fields of swarm intelligence optimization algorithms and car-following behavior modeling.

articleTitle: Efficient Serverless Resource Allocation for MapReduce Job Based on A* Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: With the development of cloud computing technology, serverless computing models have gradually emerged. The existing serverless resource allocation framework, Astrea, models the resource allocation problem as the shortest path problem in graph theory and solves it using the Dijkstra algorithm, effectively addressing resource allocation issues. However, its computational complexity can be inefficient for large-scale applications. The A* algorithm generally outperforms Dijkstra's by avoiding unnecessary paths and converging more quickly, enhancing efficiency. This paper proposes an improved A* algorithm based on the serverless job scheduling and resource allocation framework, Astrea. Implement timely budget limit checks to reduce unnecessary path exploration. Priority queues and hash tables are used to enhance data access and path query efficiency. Optimize paths with heuristic function prioritization to focus on cost-effective routes. As a result, the search space is narrowed. The Astrea framework, implemented with the A * algorithm, enhances execution efficiency. Theoretical analysis and simulation experiments confirm this, showing approximately 30% improvement compared to traditional methods. The A* algorithm is applied to serverless resource allocation. It optimizes the algorithm for large-scale MapReduce tasks. The results demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness in this new application.

articleTitle: Conjunction Screening Method for Cataloged Space Objects Based on GCN Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: As the space environment becomes increasingly congested, efficiently identifying and mitigating potential on-orbit collisions has become critical for Space Traffic Management (STM). However, the rapid growth in the number of Resident Space Objects (RSOs) presents significant challenges for accurate collision risk assessment. Advanced conjunction screening methods are essential to enhance the efficiency of collision analysis. In this study, we formulate the all-vs-all conjunction screening as a link prediction problem within the framework of Graph Neural Network (GNN). Specifically, we develop a Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) model to capture graph topology features, thereby identifying spatial dependencies between nodes. The exper-imental findings indicate that the proposed GCN model attains an F1-score of 0.8847, successfully forecasting con-junction events involving RSOs and outperforming current approaches.

articleTitle: Exponential Synchronization of Complex Spatio-Temporal Networks with Reaction-Diffusion Terms via Intermittent Pinning Adaptive Control
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: In this paper, the synchronization problem of complex spatio-temporal networks (CSNs) with reaction-diffusion terms is studied. By using Lyapunov functional method, differential inequality method and adaptive technology, the exponential synchronization of CSNs is realized by introducing intermittent pinning adaptive control, and the sufficient conditions for network synchronization are proposed. Finally, the feasibility of the theoretical results is verified by an illustrative example. This method not only reduces the conservatism of the control gain, but also saves the production cost. These advantages make this method have broad application prospects in the actual production process.

articleTitle: A New ROP Prediction Method Based on CNN-LSTM-Attention
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Rate of penetration (ROP) is a key factor in reducing drilling costs and optimizing drilling. However, the majority of ROP prediction methods are based on simple intelligent algorithms and traditional physical models, which ignore the relationship between deep sequences of drilling data, leading to lower prediction accuracy. To enhance the prediction accuracy of ROP, a ROP prediction model based on CNN-LSTM-Attention is proposed. Firstly, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) are adopted to extract the features of deep sequence data. Then, the attention mechanism is introduced to effectively extract key information of sequence features. Finally, the model is constructed and verified on a publicly available dataset. The results indicate that the proposed model can reduce the root mean square error (RMSE) by 38.22 % and improve the Determination coefficient (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R2$</tex>) by 21.51 % compared to the existing model.

articleTitle: Low Dimensional Anti-Disturbance Fuzzy Control for 2-D Spatial Parabolic PDE Systems with Nonlinear ODE Exosystem via Fuzzy Disturbance Observer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: A design method of low dimensional anti-disturbance fuzzy control via fuzzy disturbance observer (FDO) is proposed for a class of 2-dimensional (2-D) spatial nonlinear parabolic partial differential equation (PDE) systems with multiple time-domain disturbances including the disturbance modeled by the nonlinear ordinary differential equation (ODE) exosystem. First, the modal decomposition technique is applied to the PDE system to derive a low dimensional slow subsystem, which is subsequently approximated by a T-S fuzzy model. Next, a radial basis function (RBF) fuzzy system is employed and then an FDO is developed to estimate the modeled disturbance. Based on T-S fuzzy model and FDO, a low dimensional anti-disturbance fuzzy control method is developed to satisfy the uniformly ultimately boundedness (UUB). Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed design method is demonstrated on the control of a diffusion-reaction system.

articleTitle: A PSO-based Surrogate-Assisted Federated Feature Selection Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: High-dimensional feature selection (FS) problems face challenges such as the “curse of dimensionality” and high computational costs. In addition, a large amount of high-dimensional data describing the same learning task may be horizontally distributed among different institutions (called participants) and cannot be shared because of privacy protection limitations, further increasing the difficulty of high-dimensional FS problems. Therefore, a surrogate-assisted federated evolutionary FS algorithm based on particle swarm optimization (PSO) is proposed to solve the FS problem of high-dimensional data with multi-party participation under privacy protection. First, a joint filtered FS method based on the XGBoost model is proposed, which significantly reduces the initial space of features while ensuring privacy. Subsequently, a surrogate-assisted federated evolutionary FS algorithm framework under privacy protection is designed, and based on this framework, a joint construction and management strategy for the surrogate model, a joint evaluation strategy based on the surrogate model, and a joint update strategy for particles are developed. Finally, the proposed algorithm is applied to 10 test datasets, and compared with two typical evolutionary FS algorithms. The experimental results show that the proposed algorithm can not only ensure the classification performance but also significantly improve the efficiency of the algorithm while protecting the privacy of the participant data.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Surrogate Model Based on Residual Bottleneck Block for History Matching
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: History matching is a key link to predict the development performance of oil field by using reservoir numerical simulation, which directly determines the reliability of numerical simulation results. In practical application, the historical fitting process calls the numerical simulator for many times, which makes it have some problems such as heavy workload, long time consumption and expensive calculation of the numerical simulator. In order to solve the above problems, this paper constructs an RRBB-U-Net proxy model based on residual bottleneck block (RRBB) and cyclic coding-decoding network (R-U-Net) for dynamic reservoir prediction. In the aspect of parameterization of geological model, this paper combines CVAE with principal component analysis (PCA) to construct a CVAE-PCA parameterized model for the realization of two-dimensional complex perme-ability field. Finally, this paper combines RRBB-U-Net with CVAE-PCA to solve the problem of historical fitting, and combines particle swarm optimization to carry out historical fitting. The results show that the combination of the two algorithms can improve the efficiency of historical fitting and further promote the related research of reservoir historical matching.

articleTitle: Multi-scale Feature Distribution Prediction Decoder for Lightweight Monocular Depth Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Recently, various lightweight monocular depth estimation methods have been proposed. However, most methods mainly emphasize designing complex encoders while employing simple bilinear upsampling and convolution structures for decoders. That may degrade the performance of depth estimation. To address this problem, we propose a novel decoder based on image-guided multi-scale distribution prediction upsampler for lightweight monocular depth estimation. Specifically, through a distribution prediction block, our decoder predicts the distribution for every scale feature and upsamples them. The block fuses guidance and features to predict the distribution for features at higher resolutions. The feature at the lower resolutions are then upsampled to higher resolutions by a convolution-like structure, with the distribution serving as weights. Furthermore, our proposed decoder features an adaptive structure, allowing it to be combined with either single-scale or multi-scale encoders to form monocular depth estimation networks. In our experiments, we propose two networks by combining the decoder with single-scale and multi-scale encoders. Then supervised and self-supervised training of the two networks are conducted respectively. Experimental results show that our decoder has higher accuracy regardless of supervised or self-supervision training, and whether the encoder is single-scale or multi-scale. Moreover, compared with the simple decoders, our proposed decoder maintains a comparative number of parameters.

articleTitle: Unsupervised Feature Selection via Multi-Structure Learning and Indicator Matrix
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Traditional feature selection methods usually only consider a specific geometric structure of the original data, which cannot reveal the most essential underlying structure of the data. Apart from this, a regularization constraint with sparsity is often imposed on the mapping matrix, which inevitably leads to additional parameter setting issues. To address these challenges, a novel unsupervised feature selection via multi-structure learning and indicator matrix (UFSMI) is proposed in this study. More concretely, we construct a unified framework that incorporates multi-structure learning and feature selection. UFSMI first explores the global and local geometric structure of high dimensional data in subspace to excavate the intrinsic structure of data, effectively reducing the interference of redundant features. Then, an indicator matrix for feature selection that can explicitly indicate which features should be selected is in-troduced without imposing any regularization constraints. Finally, the most useful subset of features can be obtained based on the indices of the non-zero elements in the indicator matrix. A series of experiments are conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method on nine real-word high dimensional datasets by comparing with existing state-of-the-art feature selection methods.

articleTitle: Dual Sparse Variational Autoencoder-driven Interactive Estimation of Distribution Algorithm with User Generated Contents
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Personalized search and recommendation tasks in a big data environment have attracted wide attention from researchers while also presenting significant challenges.This paper proposed a dual sparse variational autoencoder-driven interactive estimation of distribution algorithm with user generated contents, which considers digging deeper into user generated contents and combining with intelligent evolutionary optimization methods. Firstly, user generated contents in web are extensively collected to build a user interest preference model based on dual sparse variational autoencoders to extract users' preference features. Secondly, the distribution probability is reconstructed according to the neurons of the output layer of the sparse variational autoencoders in the user interest preference model. Combining with Gaussian probability density function, a estimation of distribution sampling probability model based on the user interest preferences is designed in the framework of an interactive estimation of distribution algorithm to generate new individuals with the user preference information. Meanwhile, a user evaluation surrogate model based on the user interest preferences is established by integrating matrix factorizations to participate in a personalized evolutionary search process. Finally, according to new user generated contents and model management mechanisms, the user interest preference model and related models are dynamically updated to guide the interactive personalized evolutionary search for personalized recommendation task. Extensive experiments on various actual public datasets are executed to validate the feasibility, effectiveness and interpretability of the proposed algorithm. It improves the performance of personalized search and recommendation methods.

articleTitle: SSEAP: Semantic-Syntactic Enhanced Adversarial Repair for Universal Text Defense
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Designing robust defense strategies against adversarial attacks is critical for enhancing the robustness of large-scale pre-trained natural language models. Existing defense methods can generally be categorized into proactive and passive defenses. However, these methods are often tailored to specific attack algorithms or introduce new perturbations during the adversarial removal process, resulting in insufficient accuracy and generalization. To address these issues, this paper proposes the Semantic-Syntactic Enhanced Adversarial Repair for Universal Text Defense (SSEAP), a framework designed to achieve both universal and accurate text defense. Specifically, SSEAP integrates semantic and syntactic constraints into a text-denoising model. The semantic consistency constraint is designed to handle character and word-level adversarial perturbations, such as synonym replacements and word order changes. The syntactic dependency constraint is primarily employed to repair structural adversarial attacks at the sentence level. By combining these two approaches, SSEAP effectively counters various types of adversarial attacks while maintaining higher defense accuracy. We conducted extensive experiments on three popular text classification datasets, successfully defending against seven different adversarial attack algorithms. The experimental results demonstrate that SSEAP significantly outperforms existing methods in terms of both universal and accuracy (with an average AUA improvement of 22.76%).

articleTitle: CR-DIS: An Efficient Heuristic Algorithm for Minimum Weighted Vertex Cover Problem
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: The minimum weighted vertex cover (MWVC) problem is a well-known NP-hard combinatorial optimization problem. In this problem, each vertex of the graph is assigned a positive weight, and the objective is to identify a set of vertices such that every edge is covered by at least one vertex from the set, while minimizing the sum of all vertices' weights in the set. It has greater generality and broader applications than the minimum vertex cover (MVC) problem. Due to its NP-hard nature, efficiently solving the MWVC problem is a significant challenge. This paper introduces a highly efficient heuristic algorithm named CR-DIS for MWVC, which consists of two components: a construction with reductions and a dynamic improvement search framework. We compare CR-DIS with three state-of-the-art algorithms on a large number of graphs. Experimental results indicate that CR-DIS performs at a superior level, especially on large sparse graphs, yielding more best solutions and, in many instances, achieving smaller solutions with similar running times.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Discovery of Nonlinear Dynamical Systems from Noisy and Sparse Observations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics (SINDy) is a data-driven algorithm for interpretability mod-eling. SINDy has a strong ability to learn dynamical systems from time series data. Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics (SINDy) can extract equations from data, but its performance will degrade when data has noise or sparse. In order to deal with this case, the idea of Monte Carlo Markov Chain (MCMC) is introduced, which is used to optimally select models. The SINDy with MCMC (MCMC-SINDy) can comprehensively discover model structures by employing random samples in data space. Simulation results show that MCMC-SINDy is more robust than SINDy with 1 % -15 % levels of noise or sparse 0.5. These results are promising for the discovery of governing equations for complex systems in neuroscience, power grids, epidemiology, finance or ecology, where governing equations have remained elusive. mportantly, compared to existing machine learning methods, the accuracy of modeling using MCMC SINDy is higher.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Pythagorean Fuzzy Distance Method with Application in the Selection of Renewable Energy Source via MCDA
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Many complex decision-making processes have been prosecuted with the aid of Pythagorean fuzzy distance methods. This is because the theory of Pythagorean fuzzy sets has the ability to handle the vagueness and imprecision in decision-making. Various Pythagorean fuzzy distance methods have been constructed and applied to multiple criteria decision-making. Recently, Thakur et al. developed a Pythagorean fuzzy distance method based on Euler's number by considering an incomplete number of the parameters of Pythagorean fuzzy sets. This exclusion could render the result of the distance method unreliable in real-life applications. In this work, we augment the Thakur et al:'s Pythagorean fuzzy distance method by the inclusion of the complete parameters of Pythagorean fuzzy sets for an effective interpretation. The properties of the enhanced Pythagorean fuzzy distance method are described and the method satisfies the conditions of distance function. In addition, the new method is used to discuss the selection of renewable energy source based on multiple criteria decision-making approach. Furthermore, the enhanced method is compared with other existing Pythagorean fuzzy distance methods via multiple criteria decision-making approach to show the superiority of the augmented method.

articleTitle: A Reinforcement Learning-based Knowledge Graph Reasoning Verification Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: To address more complex problems and enhance the effectiveness of reasoning paths, multi-hop reasoning methods utilizing reinforcement learning have gained significant attention recently. Multi-hop reasoning aims to predict missing relationships or identify the correct answer entity by exploring multiple triples in a knowledge graph. However, existing methods often overlook the semantic information of intermediate reasoning paths, which could enhance answer accuracy, resulting in incorrect paths. Additionally, in complex scenarios, the action search space grows exponentially with more reasoning hops, drastically reducing task efficiency. This paper proposes a Reinforcement Path Reasoning Verification (RPRV) method that integrates reinforcement learning techniques. By implementing a hop limitation strategy and incorporating additional path reward signals into the reward function, this method addresses incorrect reasoning paths and improves search efficiency. These adjustments ensure that the model remains close to the initial entity during reasoning, enhancing both answer accuracy and path interpretability. Experimental results demonstrate that the model performs well on three publicly available benchmark datasets, significantly improving knowledge graph reasoning efficiency and prediction accuracy through the path validator.

articleTitle: Competition-Driven Equilibrium Optimizer with Boundary Control for Numerical Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Metaheuristic optimization algorithms are widely utilized to solve a broad range of scientific and engineering problems due to their less problem dependence, flexibility, and derivative-free mechanism. Among these, the Equilibrium Optimizer (EO) stands out as a physics-based algorithm grounded in the control volume mass balance model, demonstrating competitive performance against other advanced algorithms. However, the original EO algorithm has some limitations, such as insufficient exploitation capability, a tendency to get stuck in local optima, and an imbalance between exploration and exploitation in complex landscapes. To address these issues, this study introduces an enhanced version of the EO algorithm, called the Competitive-based Equilibrium Optimizer (CBEO). This enhancement includes a novel competition-based learning strategy that establishes a dynamically adaptive mechanism, allowing individuals to compete based on their fitness values. Additionally, a boundary control strategy has been developed to intelligently manage the behavior of individuals at the search space boundaries. The integration of these strategies significantly improves population diversity and global search capability. The exploration and exploitation capabilities of CBEO are further assessed through theoretical analysis and empirical comparisons with 12 other leading optimizers on CEC’ 17 benchmark functions. The experimental and statistical results demonstrate the competitive performance of the proposed algorithm, particularly in terms of solution quality and computational efficiency.

articleTitle: A Channel-Attention Convolutional Neural Network for Protein-DNA Binding Residue Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Accurately identifying protein-DNA binding residues is important for protein function annotation and drug design. Previous studies have used classic machine learning algorithms like support vector machines (SVMs) and random forest (RF) to predict protein-DNA binding residues. However, as new machine learning techniques are being developed, the prediction performance could be further improved. In this paper, a convolutional neural network (CNN) based framework is proposed for protein-DNA binding residues prediction, named Se-Residual-Inception network, which includes stacked Inception blocks with short-cut connection and channel-attention mechanism. We examine the performance of proposed Se-Residual-Inception network on the benchmark dataset and independent testing set, and achieve the area under the ROC curve (AUC) values of 0.882 and 0.848, respectively. The prediction performance indicates that our proposed method can precisely identify the DNA binding residues in protein sequences, which can provide assistive directions for wet-lab experiments.

articleTitle: Split Attention Mechanism of Faster RCNN for PCB Defect Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: With the development of the electronics industry, the structure of printed circuit boards (PCBs) has become increasingly complex, making defect detection a crucial part of the production process. Existing PCB detection technologies face challenges such as difficulty in detecting minor defects and positional deviation. To address these issues, this paper proposes the SP-Faster RCNN network for real-time and accurate identification and localization of small defects on PCBs. Based on Faster RCNN, this network employs Resnet50 with a split attention mechanism combined with FPN as the feature extraction network, enhancing the message passing ability for features in different scales. Additionally, K-means clustering and GIOU are utilized to make the network more suitable for the identification and localization of small defects. Experimental results show that the SP-Faster RCNN network achieves an accuracy of 98.1 % on the dataset, with a detection speed of 1.34s per iteration, meeting the practical detection requirements of PCB industrial production.

articleTitle: A Two-channel Intent Recognition Algorithm Based on Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Intention recognition is a crucial process in semantic analysis and can be viewed as a text classification task. Traditional convolutional neural networks, such as TextCNN, effectively capture local features. However, they struggle to capture contextual information and fully understand the semantic content of the text. In contrast, text convolutional recurrent neural networks (TextrCNNs) can capture long-term dependencies. This paper proposes a two-channel intention recognition algorithm named GTT. The GTT algorithm combines the strengths of TextCNN and TextRCNN, allowing it to fuse local and global features. As a result, it effectively extracts semantic information from the text, leading to a better understanding of the intent behind user queries. In the THUNews public dataset, the GTT model achieved an accuracy of 88.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>. It also recorded an accuracy rate of 90.2% and a recall rate of 88.3%. The F1 score was 87.9%. Overall, the model outperformed GloVe-CNN, GloVe-BiLSTM, and ELMo-CNN-BiGRU. These results demonstrate that the GTT model excels in extracting semantic information and understanding user intentions.

articleTitle: The Evaluation of Milling Processes Based on Fuzzy Logic
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Process evaluation and optimization are critical aspects of manufacturing, however research in this area faces challenges due to the complexity of parameter variability, strong coupling effects, and significant randomness in the machining process. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a method for assessing machining risks using fuzzy logic. First, a Type-2 fuzzy logic system was applied to fuzzify machining parameters, enabling the knowledge-based expression of these parameters. Next, an expert knowledge base for machining risks was established, with rule weights determined by an expert confidence index. The Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) was then used to identify primary and secondary risk indicators, and a fuzzy comprehensive evaluation method was employed to assess overall machining risks. Finally, a machining experiment was designed to validate the effectiveness of the risk assessment system. The experimental results demonstrate that the fuzzy logic approach effectively identifies and categorizes various machining risks, providing robust support for optimizing machining parameters and enhancing process safety.

articleTitle: An Efficient and Credible Prediction Network for High-Dimensional Critical Care Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Medical data prediction represents a key area of AI in medicine, where it plays a significant role in early disease detection and supports doctors' decision-making. With the continuous development of medical information systems, revealing more complex heterogeneous features and interrelationships among them. Existing methods that rely on manual feature engineering depend heavily on doctors' prior knowledge, which impedes the efficient prediction of patient diagnosis and prognosis. To address this issue, We propose an efficient and credible prediction network (FRGN) based on graph networks. This network extracts feature relationships from data and provides explanations for prediction results. Specifically, we first embed the heterogeneous features into the same feature space. Then, we propose a graph structure initialization method tailored to the characteristics of critical care data, which applies prior constraints to the graph to enhance the model's training speed. Finally, the graph structure learner and feature relationship encoder jointly encode the relationships among features, generating high-quality node feature representations and an accurate feature relationship model for downstream tasks. We conduct experiments on four large public critical care datasets, and the results demonstrate that compared to previous methods, the proposed FRGN network achieves greater efficiency and accuracy in predictions, while elucidating a credible feature relationship structure.

articleTitle: CDOD-NET: A Crop Disease Object Detection Model Based on Haar Wavelet Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Current crop disease object detection meth-ods are limited in species scope and performance, making them unsuitable for practical agricultural applications. To address this, building an object detection model based on the YOLOv9c network to detect multiple disease types offers a potential solution. However, the original model's low detection efficiency and the irregular shapes of disease spots further diminish its effectiveness. In order to address these challenges, this paper construct a Crop Disease Object Detection Model based on Haar Wavelet Network (CDOD-NET), and construct the Multi-species Crop Diseases Object Detection (MCDOD) dataset, which includes 64 common crop diseases. CDOD-NET incorporates Arbitrary Kernel Convolution (AKConv) to handle the irregular contours of crop diseases, Haar Wavelet Downsampling (HWD) to reduce spatial resolution while preserving critical information for faster detection, and a Global Attention Mechanism with Convolution (GAMConv) to enhance cross-dimensional fea-ture interactions, improving feature extraction. Experimental results confirm that these methods improve detection performance. On the MCDOD dataset, CDOD-NET surpass state-of-the-art methods, with improvements of 64 f/s in detection speed and 1.0% in accuracy.

articleTitle: Chronic Kidney Disease Identification Based on Multi - Modal Graph Convolutional Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a widespread and significant chronic illness with a rising global prevalence. Due to the often subtle early symptoms, many patients are diagnosed only in the later stages of the disease, making early detection and intervention crucial to slowing its progression. Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) has played a crucial role in advancing early CKD diagnosis. In this context, functional brain networks (FBNs) have attracted considerable attention as they provide insights into brain activity related to CKD. Graph convolutional networks (GCNs) have proven to be a promising method, enabling simultaneous FBN feature extraction and CKD identification while minimizing the reliance on manual feature engineering. To further enhance diagnostic accuracy, We present a multi-modal graph convolutional network (MMGCN) that incorporates various connectivity patterns. In this initial study, we combined multiple GCN modules to incorporate information from distinct connectivity patterns and evaluated the MMGCN approach using rs-fMRI scans from 100 subjects. The experimental findings demonstrate that our model achieved an 85.0 % accuracy, highlighting its potential in improving CKD diagnosis.

articleTitle: Many-Objective Evolutionary Algorithm Based on Spectral Clustering and Population Distribution
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Numerous real-world applications involve complex many-objective optimization problems characterized by a large number of objective functions. Despite the development of various algorithms to address this kind of problems, these approaches often suffer from insufficient selection pressure, complex Pareto front shapes, and uneven distribution of solutions. To address this issue, this paper introduces a many-objective evolutionary algorithm based on spectral clustering and population distribution. We first utilize spectral clustering to classify the objective functions based on their correlations and aggregate them within the same class to reducing the complexity of the problem. Then, we propose a knowledge-guided decomposition based evolutionary algorithm to solve the simplified model. Finally, we conduct a series of comparative experiments to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed method. The experimental results indicate that our method demonstrates excellent performance across various problems.

articleTitle: An Incremental Learning Method for PV Generation Prediction Based on MMD Data Screening
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) generation has garnered significant attention due to its straightforward approach to harnessing energy. However, the inherent volatility in PV power generation poses substantial challenges to the stability and reliability of the power grid. This study introduces an incremental learning method based on Maximum Mean Discrepancy data screening (IL- MMDS) to address the declining accuracy of prediction models in dynamic environments. Incremental learning helps to mitigate the issue of catastrophic forgetting in neural networks by enabling real-time model updates, allowing the model to adapt to evolving data. The proposed method and applies the Maximum Mean Discrepancy strategy to select samples that most effectively enhance the model's predictive performance and utilizes an experience replay buffer to store representative historical data. Experimental results demonstrate that compared to four existing baseline methods, the proposed IL- MMDS method delivers superior performance in PV power generation forecasting, particularly in handling complex environmental changes, resulting in higher prediction accuracy and more stable performance.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Particle Swarm Optimization K-Means Algorithm with Quantum Behavior
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: The K-means algorithm is a partition-based clustering approach with two notable drawbacks, sensitivity to the initial center and a tendency to converge to suboptimal solutions. To address these limitations, a hybrid particle swarm optimization k-means algorithm with quantum be-havior (HQPSO-K) is proposed. The improved algorithm uses a nonlinear contraction-expansion coefficient to balance local optimization and global search. Moreover, Levy flight strategy is incorporated to further improve the particles' capability to evade local optima. Finally, the improved QPSO algorithm combined with K-means explores the search space more efficiently. The algorithm is tested with UCI data set. Experimental results demonstrate that HQPSO-K achieves superior clustering outcomes and is less sensitive to initial conditions.

articleTitle: ADLM-LWD: Adaptive Deep Learning Model for Lithology Identification from Logging- While-Drilling Data with Online Learning Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Accurate lithology identification from Logging-While-Drilling (LWD) data is crucial for optimizing drilling operations and enhancing reservoir characterization in the oil and gas industry. However, the lack of standardized datasets and the need for real-time adaptability in varying geological environments pose significant challenges. This study addresses these issues through three key contributions. First, a comprehensive dataset for lithology identification is constructed, combining LWD features with corresponding lithology labels, providing a valuable resource for deep learning applications in this field. Second, a novel deep learning model is proposed, integrating 2D convolution and bidirectional LSTM to effectively capture both spatial and temporal features of LWD data. The model demonstrates high stability and performance across various metrics in extensive cross-validation tests. Lastly, an Adaptive Incremental Learning Algorithm (AILA) is introduced, incorporating online learning mechanisms and dynamic adaptation strategies to enhance the model's real-time adaptability. These advancements contribute to more accurate and adaptive lithology identification systems, which potentially improve real-time decision-making in drilling operations and lead to more efficient and cost-effective exploration and production processes.

articleTitle: An Improved Beluga Whale Optimization Algorithm Based on Chaotic Opposition-Based Learning and Adaptive Weighting Factor
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on New Trends in Computational Intelligence (NTCI)
abstract: Beluga Whale Optimization (BWO) algorithm faces challenges such as slower convergence, lower accuracy, and instability for dealing with unimodal functions. To tackle these problems, we propose an enhanced version of Beluga Whale Optimization Algorithm (ABWO). ABWO algorithm incorporates chaotic Opposition-Based Learning (OBL) and adaptive weighting factor. We fuse Logistic and Tent chaotic mappings with OBL to ensure an even distribution of individuals in the initial solution space during initialization. Consequently, the population diversity is increased and the quality of the initial solution is better. The adaptive weighting factor <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex> is introduced in the exploitation phase. It increases and then decreases with each iteration. This adjustment enhances the guiding effect of the global optimal position on individual position updates in the early stage of BWO. It also enables the algorithm to execute more effective global searches in the middle stage. Meanwhile, the algorithm converges more quickly in the late stage. Overall, the solution accuracy and convergence stability of the algorithm are improved. On nine unimodal test functions, ABWO has better optimization and convergence performance compared with six basic algorithms. It also outperforms three improved beluga whale optimization algorithms proposed by other scholars.
